anomalies.observed: The CAN transceivers U8 and U1 have their VCC1 (pin 1, VDD) connected to net NET0071. The same net NET0071 is used for the MCP2515 controller VDD (U22 pin 18), which is a 3.3V rail.
anomalies.expected: The MCP2562 CAN transceiver requires VDD (pin 1) to be 5V (4.5–5.5V). It should be connected to the +5V rail, not to the 3.3V NET0071.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet: U8 pin 1 VCC1 tied to net NET0071; U1 pin 1 VCC1 tied to net NET0071. U22 pin 18 VDD also tied to NET0071.

Spec section 1: 'two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)' — the transceiver must be powered correctly for CAN communication.

anomalies.impact: The CAN transceivers will not operate correctly because their supply voltage is below the minimum required for the CAN driver. CAN communication on both buses will fail.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains a power-connection anomaly: both CAN transceivers have their VCC1 (VDD) pin tied to the 3.3V net NET0071 instead of the required 5V rail, which will prevent CAN communication.
